thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 fired: pg-primary connection pool saturation > 95% (alert id: PD-68214) -- https://pagerduty.example/PD-68214 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: page sent to oncall (lin) and escalation policy 'db-team'
lin: acked PD-68214 :white_check_mark: I'm on it, looking at PG metrics now
jess: saw the alert, noticed increased client connections and long lock waits in query traces. tagging in: @kai for pgbouncer tweaks and @maria for recent deploy context
kai: running quick check: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=pgbouncer -o wide` -> 2 pods, cpu < 30% but conn counters are high. `psql -h pg-primary -c "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity;"` returns 1852 connections (max_conn=2000)
maria: no infra deploys in last 30m, but a batch job ramp started around 15:03 UTC. rolling back the batch is possible but need confirmation from the jobs owner (ci-scheduler).
lin: customers reporting 502s on write-heavy endpoints. Data: write error rate increased ~12% in last 5m, median DB latency 1200ms. adding read-only fallback not ideal but might reduce load
jess: can we open pgbouncer to more connections temporarily? what's the limit on pgbouncer?
kai: pgbouncer config: `max_client_conn = 20480` but pod CPU/conn handling seems bottlenecked per pod. Quick mitigation: scale pgbouncer replicas to 4 -> `kubectl scale deploy pgbouncer -n prod --replicas=4` and increase `pool_size` in runtime-config if needed. I'll do the scale now
kai: ✅ scaled pgbouncer to 4 replicas (triggered HPA override). watching metrics...
incident-bot: deploy-bot: scale started for deployment/pgbouncer (manifest v1.8) by kai at 15:12:34 UTC
omar: heads up, if pgbouncer scaling doesn't absorb, we should enable read-only fallback on the API gateway for write endpoints and surface a 'degraded writes' banner. I can flip gate if we decide
lin: currently connections dropped to ~1200 after scale but still seeing spikes that push to 1700 intermittently. CPU on pg-primary spiked; investigating active queries for long-running ones
jess: adding query sample: `SELECT * FROM events WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100` from worker-queue is scanning large partitions, taking 3-6s each, multiple workers saturating DB
maria: I'm messaging ci-scheduler owner to throttle the batch ramp. ETA for stop ack ~3m
ci-scheduler-bot: job-surface-roller has been paused by @sasha at request of @maria (reason: emergency DB mitigation)
lin: good, we see gradual decline in active connections. write error rate down to 4%. Customer impact: degraded writes for ~40 minutes, mostly affecting webhook delivery and background job completion. Not a full outage but high error rate for critical flows. Need to notify SRE and product if we keep degraded mode >1h
kai: also observed many idle clients on pgbouncer; issuing `pgbouncer -R reload` to refresh pools (doing graceful reload)
kai: reload complete, connection churn reduced, avg response latency for DB calls down to ~300ms
jess: summary for handoff: root cause - sudden ramp of batch workers + inefficient job queries -> PG saturation + pgbouncer per-pod bottleneck. Mitigations applied: scaled pgbouncer replicas -> reduced connection pressure, paused job ramp, reloaded pgbouncer, temporarily throttled writers via API fallback considered but not enabled. Current status: stable-ish, watch for recurrence.
lin: handing off to omar for overlap shift. omar, next steps: keep watch for retry storms, coordinate with infra to consider increasing pg read-replica capacity for background jobs, follow up with batch owners on query optimization. Playbook: https://internal.playbooks/redwood/db-conn-surge (runbook section 3)
omar: acked handoff. I'll keep pagerduty on-call until 16:30 UTC. Will open a brief incident note and file a postmortem if we see repeat in 24h. tagging product for customer comms: @product-oncall
jess: for postmortem: capture queries, job schedule, and pgbouncer scaling thresholds + decision timeline. I'll stash metrics and Grafana dashboards (link: https://grafana.internal/d/pg/pg-overview?orgId=1)
lin: closing PD-68214? anyone object if I resolve the page as mitigated and create follow-up ticket?
omar: go ahead, resolve it and set follow-up to TICKET-4589 (DB: investigate job ramp safeguards + long-running query cpus)
lin: resolved PD-68214 :white_check_mark: notes: mitigations applied, watch on for 2h, handoff to omar.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-68214 marked RESOLVED by lin at 15:22:39 UTC
omar: leaving thread, will update if anything changes. thanks all :heart:
